title: Composable routing playbook — sales deck (iter 1)
summary: Early draft sales deck to help AE/SEs explain composable routing (latency/cost/region/fallback policies) and to provide objection handling, one-page partner checklist, and a short ROI example for evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment choices.
content:
Slide 1 — Title
Composable routing playbook: why routing matters for revenue and reliability (iter 1)
Speaker note: Quick 2-min framing: routing is the lever that lets product teams optimize latency, availability, and cost without changing prompts or model weights.

Slide 2 — The customer problem
- Product teams hit unpredictable latency at scale when a single model endpoint is the only option
- Cost blowups from naive scaling (over-provisioning GPUs)
- Region or compliance constraints require fallback strategies
- Customers often ask: how do we guarantee 99% p95 under load?

Slide 3 — Redwood value prop (routing lens)
- Unified API across Hosted / Dedicated / Private with routing policies
- Route by: latency SLO, unit cost, model capability, region, and customer tier
- Automatic fallback to compatible variants when capacity constrained
- Prefix/KV caching + smart batching reduces per-token cost while respecting latency SLOs

Slide 4 — How composable routing works (simple flow)
- Inbound request -> policy evaluation
- Priority: region match -> customer pinned version -> latency tier -> cost tier -> fallback list
- If primary route rejects (high queue/latency), switch to next compatible variant (e.g., quantized or smaller architecture)
- Circuit-breaker and transient cooldowns for noisy upstreams

Slide 5 — Objection handling examples (AE/SE scripts)
Obs: "We can't risk a lower-quality model on fallback"
- Reply: Explain canary and A/B rollout; show SLOs per route and how rollouts keep traffic split 1-5% to validate quality first
- Quick stat: typical accuracy regression with our 4-bit quantized fallback is <2% on common summarization prompts (internal benchmark)

Obs: "We need absolute p95 guarantees"
- Reply: We recommend Dedicated + routing policy pinned to latency-tier nodes; if first-tier capacity reached, automatic fallback to higher-latency-but-cheaper region or reserve burst pool (configurable).

Slide 6 — Competitor notes (talking points)
- Cloud X: simple geo-routing but no model-variant fallbacks or automatic cache-aware batching
- Vendor Y: offers on-prem runtime but lacks unified control plane and rollout policies
- Selling angle: Redwood combines runtime-level optimizations (batching, KV caching) with policy orchestration — lowers unit cost without sacrificing reliability

Slide 7 — Example customer scenario (SaaS search product)
- Baseline: single hosted endpoint, p95 = 420ms under load, cost per 1M tokens = $540
- With composable routing: route high-priority queries to low-latency pool, long-form/low-priority to cheaper quantized pool -> p95 for critical queries = 120ms, blended cost = $360 per 1M tokens (33% savings)
- ROI callout: for a customer doing 50M tokens/mo, annual savings ~ $108k; engineering ops cost to run Dedicated reserved pool estimated $25k/yr -> net win for Reserved/Dedicated discussion

Slide 8 — Deck appendix: routing policy examples
- Latency-first policy (enterprise): prefer nodes with p95 < 150ms, fallback list: same-region quantized -> cross-region low-latency pool -> burst reserved pool
- Cost-first policy (startup): prefer cheapest compatible model unless request meta indicates critical low-latency flag; cache TTLs increased for repeated prompts

Slide 9 — Quick technical FAQ for SEs
Q: How are model variants validated?
A: We run per-customer prompt sets in sandbox canary and compute quality deltas, surface regressions in Evaluate -> Rollout console
Q: What about KV cache correctness?
A: Cache keys salted by customer id + prompt fingerprint; invalidation via rollout tag when model changes.

Slide 10 — One-page checklist for discovery call
- Is latency a hard SLO or a preference? (ask for p50/p95 targets)
- Typical token count and request concurrency patterns? (burstiness)
- Regulatory constraints: region-specific or air-gapped?
- Will they accept minor quality delta on fallback? (threshold %)
- Budget / unit-cost sensitivity and preferred billing model (usage vs reserved)

Slide 11 — Example playbook script (cold call / discovery)
- Open: "Are you seeing unexpected latency spikes at scale or paying for idle GPU capacity?"
- If yes: "We recommend a short pilot that routes critical traffic to a latency-optimized pool, and lower-priority workloads to a quantized pool. We can show a cost/latency delta in 2-3 days with a small traffic split."

Slide 12 — Metrics to show in demo
- p50/p95 latency per route, cost per 1000 tokens by route, cache hit ratio, fallbacks triggered per hour, model-quality delta for canary traffic

Slide 13 — Open questions / TODOs (internal)
